judge_llm: Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct via HF Inference Providers (featherless-ai) -- same model this project's HuggingFaceProvider uses for real generation
embeddings: all-MiniLM-L6-v2 -- same local model the retrieval pipeline itself runs on

history.label: before fix -- fixed_size_chunks (200-word sliding window, 40-word overlap)
history.finding: The DPDP consent question retrieved the wrong chunk. Root cause: a real retrieval miss, not a generation hallucination -- the correct chunk (containing the exact 'free, specific, informed, unconditional, unambiguous' text) exists in the corpus (1 of 379 chunks) but never ranked in the top-15 dense-retrieval candidates for this query. The chunk itself spliced the tail of an unrelated notice-language clause together with the start of Section 6, diluting its embedding relevance. This was a chunking-boundary quality issue, not a bug in re-ranking or the sufficiency gate -- both correctly did their job on the (wrong) chunks they were given.

history.label: after fix -- semantic_chunks (blank-line paragraph boundaries, >=5-word filter)
history.finding: Fix verified for real, not assumed: re-ran retrieve_pdf_chunks for the exact same failing query against the rebuilt corpus (1021 chunks, up from 379) -- the Section 6(1) consent clause now ranks #1 (score 0.987), cleanly isolated with no splicing. All three RAGAS answers are now correct against their ground truths. Full pytest suite re-run after the corpus rebuild: still 27/30 passing, same pre-existing Claude-billing failures, no regressions from the chunking change.

history.label: after fix, confirmed against production -- redeployed HF Space with the rebuilt chroma_data/
history.methodology_note: answer is a genuine round-trip through the deployed Space's live /agent/run endpoint (eval/ragas_eval.py --production); contexts are reconstructed via local retrieve_pdf_chunks against the same chroma_data/ that was just redeployed (verified byte-identical -- the API doesn't expose raw retrieved-chunk text, only source filenames, so this is the one piece not a direct API round-trip). Retrieval is deterministic given the same corpus + embedding model + query, so this reflects exactly what production's own internal retrieval used.
history.finding: All three production answers are correct against ground truth, including the previously-failing DPDP consent question. Scores consistent with the local post-fix run (small faithfulness/answer_relevancy variance is expected -- each is a fresh, non-deterministic LLM generation; context_precision/recall match exactly since they depend only on the corpus, which is identical).

fix_details.root_cause: ingestion/build_corpus.py used fixed_size_chunks (ingestion/chunking.py): a naive 200-word sliding window with 40-word overlap, oblivious to sentence/section boundaries -- it mechanically sliced across a real section boundary in DPDP_Act_2023.pdf.
fix_details.fix: Switched to the existing (previously unused) semantic_chunks function: splits on Docling's blank-line paragraph boundaries, which for these structured government PDFs already isolate each numbered clause/sub-section into its own paragraph (verified directly against the real extracted markdown). Added a >=5-word minimum filter to semantic_chunks after confirming every one of DPDP_Act_2023.pdf's 55 sub-5-word paragraphs was pure structural noise (chapter headers, '## Illustration.' markers, Hindi gazette boilerplate, bare cross-reference citations like '24 of 1997.') -- none of them real content.
fix_details.deployment_note: Deployed -- the HF Space was redeployed with the rebuilt chroma_data/ and the fix is confirmed live (see the 'confirmed against production' history entry above).
